applies_why: The judge uses a both-senses-standing rationale to label a challenge UNDERDETERMINED, which is the openness K-S2 governs.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- C5 bounds Isaiah’s sign with Isaiah 7:16 and 8:3-4 and notes *‘almah* (young woman), while D5 also rests on Matthew 1:23 *parthenos* (virgin); [CR2] G answered the sign rows. GROUND: the near sign and Matthew’s virgin application are both left standing.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. I weighed whether both senses standing forbids an UNDERDETERMINED label or instead leaves the matter open; K-S2 says such a verse is not open.
why: The judge marks D5 vs C5 UNDERDETERMINED because the near sign and Matthew’s virgin application are both left standing, which treats a two-sense verse as open contrary to K-S2.
